summary.title: Documenting Architecture Decisions
summary.one_liner: Architecture Decision Records (ADRs): short, numbered, version-controlled documents that capture the context and rationale behind significant architecture decisions so future developers don't blindly accept or reverse them.
keywords: keeping docs up to date agile
takeaways: Keep architecture decision records small, modular, and in the project repository (e.g. doc/arch/adr-NNN.md) so they stay up to date.
Use a short format with Title, Context, Decision, Status, and Consequences, written as full sentences in active voice.
Number records sequentially and never reuse numbers; mark reversed decisions as superseded rather than deleting them.
Record the forces and rationale behind decisions so new team members avoid blindly accepting or reversing them.
Cognitect reported positive early feedback from developers rotating through projects, and used ADRs to capture longer-term intentions.
summary.summary: Cognitect describes why they adopted Architecture Decision Records for agile projects: small, modular documents that record the forces, the decision, its status, and its consequences. Each ADR is a short Markdown or Textile file kept in the repo, numbered sequentially, and superseded rather than deleted when reversed. The post reports early experience over a few months with six to ten rotating developers, who valued the context, and notes that GitHub rendering makes the files accessible to non-developer stakeholders. It is a short opinion and experience piece with an example of the format itself.
